guarantees.claim: txcount_d holds its previous value (txcount) when no control signal (clr_txcount, load_txcount, inc_txcount) is asserted.
txcount_d is cleared to zero when clr_txcount is asserted.

On load_txcount (and not clr_txcount), txcount_d is set to message_length_i plus a digest-dependent block size constant: BlockSizeSHA256in64 for SHA2_256, BlockSizeSHA512in64 for SHA2_384 and SHA2_512, and zero for any other digest_size_i.
When inc_txcount is asserted (and neither clr nor load), bits [63:5] of txcount_d are incremented by 1, effectively adding 32 to the full txcount.

assumptions.claim: The constants BlockSizeSHA256in64 and BlockSizeSHA512in64 are correctly defined as the block sizes in 64-bit words (8 and 16 respectively).
assumptions.risk: Incorrect constant would cause wrong HMAC block length tracking, breaking message authentication.

assumptions.claim: digest_size_i is stable and valid when load_txcount is asserted.
assumptions.risk: If digest_size_i changes during load, the added block size may be stale, causing incorrect txcount_d and potential HMAC failure.

assumptions.claim: message_length_i is expressed in the same unit (64-bit words) as the block size constants.
assumptions.risk: Unit mismatch would produce a meaningless txcount_d, breaking the HMAC length tracking and security.

uncertain_points.claim: The default case in the digest_size_i unique case (line 265) sets txcount_d = message_length_i + 0. It is unclear whether digest_size_i can legally take values other than the three SHA-2 variants. If an invalid or corrupted value occurs, the block size addition is omitted, potentially undermining HMAC integrity.
uncertain_points.cond: load_txcount asserted with an unspecified digest_size_i
uncertain_points.risk: HMAC message tracking may be incorrect, allowing forgeries or data manipulation.

uncertain_points.claim: It is not locally verified that message_length_i and the block size constants (BlockSizeSHA256in64, BlockSizeSHA512in64) share the same unit (64-bit words). If message_length_i is in bytes, the addition will be wrong, causing undetected HMAC length mismatch.
uncertain_points.risk: Systematic unit mismatch could invalidate HMAC tag calculation for all messages.
